oracleRisk.summary: Tempo block 45095255 (2026-10-20T22:17:20Z) retains one adapter and one cbBTC/pathUSD market. The shared RedStone adapter implementation, newly verified on 19 October, now has source-matched executable bytecode. It requires three of five fixed RedStone signers, validates signed packages within three minutes on update, and rejects reads 30 hours after the last update. Both serial price feeds depend on this one adapter and the same 2-of-3 Safe upgrade authority; fallback updater addresses do not supply an independent price source. The topology is therefore single-source-or-laggy, not opaque or independently redundant.

branches.fallbackBehavior: The composite multiplies serial base feeds and divides serial quote feeds, with no independent alternative. The exact feed implementations call MultiFeedAdapterWithoutRounds.getLastUpdateDetails, which requires a positive value and lastBlockTimestamp + 108000 > block.timestamp. Thus reads fail closed at 30 hours; the 24-hour cbBTC and 6-hour pathUSD publisher heartbeats remain relayer targets, not the enforced bound. Newly verified TempoMultiFeedAdapterWithoutRoundsV1 requires three distinct signatures from five hardcoded RedStone addresses, median aggregation, and package timestamps no older than three minutes or more than one minute ahead at update. Main, fallback, manual and Gelato updater addresses all submit the same signed-data service; they are transport alternatives, not independent oracle failover. Current implementation and executable-source correspondence were pinned at block 45095255. Shared 2-of-3 Safe upgrade authority remains; financial recovery and actual stressed liquidation capacity are not established by this review.
